# ↪️ Pull Request

<!---

Please look for any issues that this PR resolves and tag them in the PR.

This PR ensures Parcel installls all compiler libraries for asset types in the same project (the root project).

This is for file structures where a project has multiple package.json's or a file outside of the project dir is required. (which would both resolve in re-installing the package)

This is a work in progress, still need to test this a little bit and make sure the current tests pass again

Fixes #2318

issue_context.title: Parcel cannot find dependencies when run on directory outside project
issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🐛 bug report

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue here -->

## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

Setup

```bash
set -e

# put a sass file in a 'static' dir
mkdir -p static
echo 'p { color: red }' > static/foo.scss

# put a project with parcel in another 'parcel' dir
mkdir -p parcel
cd parcel
echo '{ "devDependencies": { "parcel-bundler": "^1.10.3", "sass": "^1.15.1" } }' > package.json
npm install

# run the local parcel build
./node_modules/.bin/parcel watch ../static/foo.scss
```

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

<!--- Tell us what should happen -->

I would expect the file to build properly with parcel knowing where I called it from and to resolve the `sass` dependency from its local directory.

## 😯 Current Behavior

<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->
<!--- If you are seeing an error, please include the full error message and stack trace -->

If run from `/tmp/parcel-folders-test/`, it says it’s installing `sass` and afterwards it gives the error:

> /tmp/parcel-folders-test/static/foo.scss: Cannot find module 'sass' from '/tmp/parcel-folders-test/static'

Furthermore, if you run it as an npm script:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "start": "parcel watch ../static/foo.scss"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "parcel-bundler": "^1.10.3",
    "sass": "^1.15.1"
  }
}
```

After running it, the package.json file updates to just be:

```json
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "sass": "^1.15.1"
  }
}
```

## 💁 Possible Solution

<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix/reason for the bug -->

It seems like the parcel CLI is designed to work with a global install or a local install and it seems to resolve local dependencies by looking at the context of the file that is being bundled. It seems like it should also try to resolve dependencies based on the location of the parcel cli file too.

## 🔦 Context

<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->
<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

I was experimenting with adding parcel bundling to a django project that was using docker and was seeing if I could have a separate container do the bundling and I wanted it to be able to work on other directories.

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 1.10.3 |
| Node             | v10.11..0 |
| npm/Yarn         | 6.4.1/1.6.0 |
| Operating System | Mac OSX 10.13.6 |

<!-- Love parcel? Please consider supporting our collective:
👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->
comments:
This is how localRequire is implemented currently, we could change it to use rootDir instead of the asset path for resolving compilers.
That should probably change this (fix this) to the behaviour you expect.
Yeah, that sounds right. In the meantime, I changed the structure of things in my project to deal with it working this way.

Thank you @mrcoles for filing the bug report.  It took me a quiet a while to figure out what was happening.

I'm dropping the following line in here to hopefully help others find the issue quickly in case they have the same error message: 

```stylesheet.css:undefined:undefined: Cannot find module 'cssnano' from 'stylesheet.css' ```

Hi, thanks @mrcoles for writing such a nice issue that exactly matched what I wanted to find out. I have the same issue where a project imports a module that is one level up from the root directory.

It would be helpful behaviour IMO if the node_modules within root dir, i.e. within the dir where the build is run, be looked in when resolving dependencies for modules that are outside the directory. Understand if there are considerations that might make this harmful in certain circumstances.
I'm having the same issue. Is there a solution?
Maybe for more context. I have to manually copy some files to the tmp dir of the os and build it there. This results in my package.json getting deleted and the build failing.
